content:
I couldn't open the PR yet. The repo's trailvault commit hook stopped the commit with this message:

> trailvault: This repository requires session logs; consent is absent, declined, or its policy/origin changed. Run `trailvault consent` to review it.

That consent controls whether session logs get shared, so you should decide it. I didn't run it or skip the hook myself.

**What's ready:**
- [visualizations/bouncing-ball.html](visualizations/bouncing-ball.html) was already staged in your checkout. It's a single HTML page with gravity and bounciness sliders, pause and reset buttons, click-to-throw, a squash effect when the ball lands, a motion trail, and light and dark themes. I used it as the PR content.
- I made one fix to it. On high-resolution screens the drawing area could keep growing taller with every resize, so I added `min-height: 0` to stop that. I haven't seen the page running, because the browser pane was hidden when I tried.
- I moved the file onto a new branch, `viz/bouncing-ball`, which starts from `origin/main`. Your current branch, `demo/route-search-20261030`, has route-search commits that aren't on main, and starting from it would have added them to this PR.

To review the consent prompt, run:

```bash
trailvault consent
```

Once you've done that, I'll commit, push and open the PR against `main`. If you'd rather I commit with `--no-verify` to bypass the hook, tell me and I'll do that instead.
